name: Rhodes Scholarship (United States)
summary: Fully funded graduate degree study at the University of Oxford, covering all course fees plus a living stipend. The US constituency awards 32 scholarships a year through 16 regional committees.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES institutional endorsement — you cannot apply directly; your college/university must endorse you, and most run a competitive internal selection. Bachelor's degree must be completed before taking up the scholarship (current seniors may apply). Age limits exist but are constituency-specific and published in the annual 'Information for Candidates — USA' document; the Rhodes Trust states they are 'immovable.' No published GPA floor, but successful US candidates are overwhelmingly top-of-class.
selectivity_note: 32 US scholarships per year, awarded two each by 16 regional selection committees. Applicant-pool size not stated on the official page.
pay_note: £20,400 per annum (£1,700/month) for 2025-26, from which scholars pay all living expenses including accommodation. Also covers Oxford course fees, Oxford application fees, student visa and NHS health surcharge, two economy flights, and a settling-in allowance. 2027-28 stipend figure not yet published.

deadlines.note: Online application opens 1 July 2026.
Application closes 23:59 ET, 7 October 2026. Institutional endorsements must also be received by this same deadline.
Campus endorsement deadlines are set by each institution and run MONTHS earlier — commonly spring or early summer 2026. Students must contact their fellowships office; no single national date exists.

caveat_note: Stipend figure is the published 2025-26 rate; confirm the 2027-28 rate before publishing. Age eligibility is genuinely constituency-specific — do not publish a numeric age cap without pulling the current 'Information for Candidates — USA' PDF. Citizenship set to us_citizen; the US constituency has residency-based alternative pathways that were not verified in this pass.

name: Marshall Scholarship
summary: Funds one to three years (most commonly two) of postgraduate study at any UK university, covering full tuition plus a living stipend. Up to roughly 50 scholars are selected annually.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES institutional endorsement — applications must be submitted through an endorsing US institution, which runs its own internal competition. Minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.7 on a 4.0 scale at the time of application; rounded GPAs are NOT accepted. Degree must be from an accredited US institution, with a recent-graduation window (verify the exact year cutoff in the current Rules for Candidates).
selectivity_note: Up to 50 scholarships per year (some sources cite up to 40 in recent cycles). Applicant-pool size not confirmed from an official source.
pay_note: Covers full university tuition and fees, a living stipend, an annual book grant, a thesis grant, research and daily travel grants, return flights between the US and UK, and where applicable a dependent spouse allowance. Exact stipend rate not confirmed in this pass.

deadlines.note: Deadline for applicants and recommenders is 29 September 2026 at 5:00pm IN THE TIME ZONE OF THE ENDORSING INSTITUTION — the ISO offset here assumes Eastern; adjust for the student's school.
Institution's endorsement letter due to the Marshall Commission 1 October 2026 at 5:00pm in the endorsing institution's time zone.
Campus internal deadlines commonly fall in JULY or AUGUST 2026 — e.g. Harvard's endorsement application deadline was 21 July 2026. Varies by school; contact the fellowships office by spring.

caveat_note: Stipend amount unconfirmed. The '5:00pm in the endorsing institution's time zone' rule means a single ISO timestamp is technically wrong for non-Eastern schools — display the rule, not just the timestamp. Number awarded (40 vs 50) is inconsistent across sources; verify against marshallscholarship.org before publishing a figure.

name: George J. Mitchell Scholarship
summary: One year of postgraduate study at an institution on the island of Ireland, historically covering tuition, housing, a living stipend and travel. The US-Ireland Alliance announced in March 2024 that it was PAUSING selection of future Mitchell Scholar classes.
other_eligibility: When running: institutional endorsement REQUIRED for undergraduate applicants only — graduate students and applicants already holding a bachelor's degree at the deadline did not submit an endorsement. Campus endorsement deadlines ran earlier than the national deadline. US citizenship verified at finalist stage.
selectivity_note: Historically 12 scholars per year. Not currently selecting.
pay_note: Historically covered university tuition, accommodation/housing, a living-expenses stipend and a travel stipend. No current figures — program is paused.
funding_note: In March 2024 the US-Ireland Alliance announced its decision to pause selection of future classes of George J. Mitchell Scholars. As of August 2026 the official Application Process page still carries that notice and no new cycle is open.

deadlines.note: No open cycle. Last competition closed 28 September 2023 at 5:00pm ET for the 2024-25 class.

caveat_note: DO NOT list this as an available option without a prominent 'paused' badge. Pause confirmed directly on the US-Ireland Alliance site as of this research pass. Re-check quarterly — a restart announcement is plausible.

name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
operator: Gates Cambridge Trust / University of Cambridge
summary: Fully funded postgraduate study at the University of Cambridge, covering the full cost of studying plus a maintenance stipend. US citizens resident in the US apply in a dedicated earlier round.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — you apply directly. You must simultaneously apply for admission to a Cambridge graduate course through the University's own application, and be a US citizen RESIDENT IN THE USA at the time of application to use the US round; US citizens studying or working overseas must apply in the later international round. Open to all subjects.
selectivity_note: Approximately 25 scholarships in the US round (about 80 total per year across both rounds). Applicant-pool size not confirmed from official source.
pay_note: Maintenance stipend reported at £22,050 for 12 months (pro rata for shorter courses), plus full University Composition Fee, one economy return airfare, visa and health surcharge costs, academic development funding up to £2,000, and a family allowance up to £17,375. Stipend figure is from secondary sources, not the official timeline page.

deadlines.note: Applications open September 2026 for entry in academic year 2027/8. Exact opening date not published.
US round deadline: Wednesday 14 October 2026, 12:00am GMT. For US citizens resident in the USA. (Some third-party sites list 16 October — the official Gates Cambridge timeline page says 14 October.)
International round: either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, 12:00am GMT, DEPENDING ON THE COURSE. Check the Cambridge Course Directory for your specific program.

caveat_note: The stipend figure came from secondary sources; verify on gatescambridge.org/apply/ before publishing. The 12:00am GMT deadline is a trap — it means the END of 13 October in practice for anyone thinking in US time. Flag this.

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
summary: Funds up to three years of any graduate degree at Stanford, covering tuition and fees plus a living stipend and an annual travel stipend. Scholars join a multidisciplinary leadership development community alongside their degree program.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required. To enroll in 2027 you must have earned your first/bachelor's degree in 2020 or later (military service adds two years of eligibility). You must ALSO separately apply for and be admitted to a Stanford graduate degree program, which has its own — often different and sometimes earlier — deadline. No restrictions on age, undergraduate institution, field of study, or nationality.
selectivity_note: Roughly 80-90 scholars per cohort (87 in the 2026 cohort) from 9,223 applications for that cohort — roughly a 1% admit rate. Applicant figures from secondary reporting.
pay_note: For each of the first three years of graduate study: a fellowship applied directly to tuition and associated fees, plus a stipend for living and academic expenses (room, board, books, supplies, local transport, personal expenses), plus a travel stipend for one annual economy round trip to Stanford. Exact dollar amounts were not retrievable — the Stanford eligibility page returned HTTP 403.

deadlines.note: Knight-Hennessy application closes 6 October 2026 at 1:00pm Pacific Time, for enrollment in 2027.
SEPARATE Stanford graduate program application deadline — varies by school and department, and some fall before the KHS deadline. Applicants must track both.

caveat_note: Stipend dollar amount unverified (Stanford eligibility page blocked automated fetch — verify manually). The dual-application structure is the single biggest thing to communicate: winning KHS is meaningless without separate Stanford grad admission.

name: Churchill Scholarship
operator: Winston Churchill Foundation of the United States
summary: Funds one year of master's study in science, mathematics or engineering at Churchill College, University of Cambridge, covering all fees plus a living stipend, airfare and research grants. Total award value is stated as over $80,000.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES campus nomination — the Foundation accepts applications only from a limited list of Participating Institutions, each of which may nominate up to two candidates. You must be enrolled at a participating institution or have graduated within the 12 months before the deadline, hold a bachelor's degree by the time you take up the award, and be a US citizen (native-born or naturalized). Field restricted to science, mathematics and engineering; the two Kanders Churchill Scholarships are for science policy. Churchill College must be listed first on your Cambridge application.
selectivity_note: Up to 18 scholarships per year: 16 Churchill Scholarships in science/math/engineering plus 2 Kanders Churchill Scholarships in science policy. Each participating institution may nominate at most two candidates.
pay_note: Stated TOTAL AWARD VALUE is 'over $80,000' — this is the whole package, not take-home pay. Includes tuition/fees, a living stipend, round-trip airfare to the UK, visa fees and the health surcharge; scholars may additionally apply for a $4,000 research grant. The living-stipend component is not itemized publicly.

deadlines.note: Nomination deadline to the Winston Churchill Foundation: Monday 2 November 2026, 5:00pm ET.

Campus internal deadlines run WEEKS EARLIER and vary by school — e.g. Georgetown 21 September 2026, Penn 1 October 2026. Students must contact their institution's scholarship office; there is no way to apply directly.

caveat_note: The $80,000 figure is total award value including tuition — do not present it as a stipend. Only students at Participating Institutions can apply at all; consider surfacing a link to the Foundation's participating-institution list.

name: Harry S. Truman Scholarship
summary: A $30,000 award toward graduate or professional school for college juniors committed to careers in public service, plus leadership training and a public service alumni network. It funds a future degree — it does not pay a living stipend.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES campus nomination — each accredited four-year institution may nominate up to four students for the 2027 awards, and you cannot apply independently. You must be a full-time JUNIOR-level student at a four-year institution during the 2026-27 academic year, expecting a bachelor's degree between December 2027 and August 2028. Requires a policy proposal and three letters of recommendation. Commitment to a public service career is the core selection criterion.
selectivity_note: Each institution may nominate at most four candidates nationally. Total scholars per year and applicant-pool size not confirmed from the official source in this pass.
pay_note: $30,000 toward graduate or professional school tuition. This is education funding, not income — Truman Scholars receive no living stipend from the award.

deadlines.note: Truman application deadline 2 February 2027, 11:59pm IN THE APPLICANT'S OWN TIME ZONE. Materials-receipt confirmation 8 February 2027; finalists announced 15 February 2027; regional interviews 1 March-15 April 2027; Scholars announced 23 April 2027. The Foundation states these dates are firm and will not be changed.

Campus nomination deadlines are set by each institution's Truman Faculty Representative and typically fall in autumn 2026 — weeks to months before the national deadline. Students must start with their campus Truman advisor.

caveat_note: IMPORTANT MISMATCH: Truman is applied for as an UNDERGRADUATE JUNIOR, not post-graduation. Its stage is really 'current undergrad', and the schema's post_undergrad label is misleading here — surface the junior-year requirement prominently or the directory will send seniors and graduates to an application they cannot make. Money is tuition support for a later degree, hence net_neutral rather than participant_earns.
exclude_reason: Applied for as a junior while enrolled — a graduate-school scholarship, not a path for a year off.

name: Udall Undergraduate Scholarship
summary: Up to $7,500 for one year of undergraduate study, awarded to sophomores and juniors committed to careers in the environment, Tribal public policy, or Native American health care. It covers tuition, fees, books and room and board — it is not a stipend.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES campus nomination — only your institution's Udall faculty representative can give you access to the application; you cannot apply independently. Must be a sophomore- or junior-level undergraduate. Three tracks: environment; Tribal public policy; Native American health care. Applicants in the Tribal public policy and health care tracks, and eligible US permanent residents, must submit additional documentation.
selectivity_note: Approximately 65 scholarships of up to $7,500 each per year (figure from secondary sources; not confirmed on udall.gov in this pass).
pay_note: Up to $7,500 for one year, usable for tuition, fees, books, and room and board. Education funding, not income.
funding_note: Program appears active: the 2026 online application opened 15 October 2025 with a 4 March 2026 deadline.

deadlines.note: 2027 deadline NOT YET CONFIRMED on udall.gov. Some secondary sources cite 3 March 2027; the 2026 cycle deadline was 4 March 2026 with the application opening 15 October 2025. Expect an early-March 2027 date and verify in autumn 2026.
Campus deadlines set by each institution's Udall faculty representative, and earlier than the national date. You literally cannot access the application without your faculty rep.

caveat_note: IMPORTANT MISMATCH: Udall is a SOPHOMORE/JUNIOR undergraduate scholarship, not a post-graduate path — it does not belong in a post-undergrad directory without a clear label. The 2027 deadline is unconfirmed; do not publish the 3 March 2027 date until udall.gov posts it. Number awarded (65) is from secondary sources.
exclude_reason: Applied for as a sophomore/junior while enrolled — not a path for a year off.

name: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship)
operator: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), administered by IIE
summary: Funds intensive overseas language study in world regions critical to US national security, for undergraduates (Boren Scholarship) and graduate students (Boren Fellowship). Awards cover overseas program costs and carry a binding federal service requirement afterward.
other_eligibility: Campus review is common but the award is applied for directly through IIE; many institutions set an internal campus deadline and require a campus representative's involvement — check with your campus Boren rep. SCHOLARSHIP: must be matriculated in a US associate's or bachelor's program at time of application and stay enrolled through the award. FELLOWSHIP: must be matriculated in, or applying to, a US graduate degree program by the fellowship start date — enrollment is not required at the time of application. US citizenship required. You may not study in a country where you hold citizenship. Programs must include at least 15-20 weekly language contact hours. Carries a federal service requirement (work for a national-security-relevant federal agency).
selectivity_note: Award counts and applicant-pool figures not confirmed from official sources in this pass.
pay_note: Scholarship (undergrad): $8,000 for an 8-11 week summer program (STEM majors only), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, $25,000 for 25-52 weeks. Fellowship (grad): $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, $25,000 for 25-52 weeks, plus optionally up to $12,000 for domestic summer intensive language study, to a combined maximum of $30,000. Funds are designed to cover the majority of overseas expenses — this is cost coverage, not income. Amounts from secondary sources; verify on borenawards.org.

deadlines.note: Boren FELLOWSHIP (graduate) national deadline: 20 January 2027, 5:00pm ET.
Boren SCHOLARSHIP (undergraduate) national deadline: 27 January 2027, 5:00pm ET.
Many institutions set their own earlier internal deadline and require campus-representative review. Dates vary; contact your campus Boren representative in autumn 2026.

caveat_note: The federal service requirement is a real, contractual obligation and is the thing students most often miss — surface it prominently. This entry merges two distinct awards with different deadlines and different eligibility; consider splitting into two directory entries. Neither is a post-graduation gap-year path in the usual sense: the Scholarship is for enrolled undergrads, the Fellowship for grad students. Award amounts are from secondary sources.

name: Critical Language Scholarship (CLS) Program
operator: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs
summary: A fully funded eight-to-ten-week summer intensive language institute abroad in one of nine critical languages, delivering roughly a year of language study. All major costs are covered plus a small daily-living stipend.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly. You MUST be enrolled in an accredited US degree-granting program (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral or professional) and enrolled in at least one credit-bearing class in the fall term preceding the program; enrollment in the following spring term is also required unless you graduate that December. Graduating seniors and students in one-year master's programs ARE eligible. Must be a US citizen or national and at least 18 by the program start. Open to all academic disciplines.
selectivity_note: Approximately 315 US undergraduate and graduate students selected for the 2026 program from a pool of more than 4,500 applicants (roughly 7%).
pay_note: Covers travel between the US, Washington DC and the program country; visa application fees; language instruction; room and board; program-sponsored travel; US academic credit; and the Oral Proficiency Interview assessment. Includes a small stipend for daily living expenses — amount not published.
funding_note: Program ran a full 2026 cycle (approximately 315 participants). The official site states the 2027 application will be available in Fall 2026.

deadlines.note: Official CLS site: 'The application for the 2027 CLS Program will be available Fall 2026.' No exact opening date published as of this research pass.

2027 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED. Historical pattern: applications open mid-September with a mid-to-late November deadline (the 2026 cycle closed 18 November 2025 at 8:00pm ET). Verify in autumn 2026 — do not publish an estimated date.

caveat_note: MISMATCH: CLS requires CURRENT enrollment in a US degree program — it is a summer program for enrolled students, not a post-graduation gap-year option. Graduating seniors qualify only for the summer immediately following graduation. Also: as a State Department ECA program it is exposed to federal budget action; the 2026 cycle ran normally but re-verify status before each cycle.
exclude_reason: Requires current enrollment and runs 8-10 weeks over a summer — not a year-off path.

name: Yenching Academy of Peking University
summary: A fully funded interdisciplinary master's in China Studies at Peking University in Beijing, covering tuition, housing, round-trip travel and a monthly stipend. Roughly 120 scholars enroll each year, about three quarters of them international.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly. Must hold at least a bachelor's degree, or be enrolled in a bachelor's program and on track to graduate no later than 31 August 2027. International applicants must be non-Chinese citizens holding a valid foreign passport; former citizens of Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan must document their change of citizenship as of before 30 April 2021. Requires an outstanding academic record, strong English proficiency, and demonstrated interest in interdisciplinary China studies. Chinese language ability is not required for admission.
selectivity_note: Approximately 120 new students enrolled annually, roughly 75% international. Applicant-pool size not published.
pay_note: The Academy states it provides a fellowship to all scholars covering tuition, housing (on-campus accommodation or an off-campus housing stipend), a monthly stipend, round-trip travel and field study expenses, plus basic medical insurance. The monthly stipend amount is NOT published on the official admissions page; secondary sources describe it as roughly USD 500 equivalent — unverified.

deadlines.note: Official admissions page: 'Recruitment information for the 2027 cohort will be available around September.' No dates published as of this research pass.
2027 deadline not yet announced. Historically the international round has run from autumn with deadlines in the winter/early spring. Verify from September 2026.

caveat_note: Stipend amount unverified — do not publish a dollar figure. Program length (1 vs 2 years) was not confirmed on the fetched page; the term range here is an estimate and should be verified. Set to participant_earns because tuition, housing and travel are covered AND a monthly stipend is paid, but if the stipend turns out to be nominal, net_neutral would be more honest.

name: Coro Fellows Program in Public Affairs
operator: Coro (regional centers: Los Angeles, Bay Area, New York, St. Louis, Pittsburgh)
summary: A nine-month, full-time experiential leadership program in public affairs, rotating fellows through placements in government, business, labor, nonprofits and political campaigns. The program is tuition-free, but living stipends are limited, need-based and vary sharply by regional center.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required. Two-stage selection: a written application followed by a full-day in-person 'Selection Day' assessment. Each regional center recruits and selects separately, with its own stipend policy — you apply to a specific city. Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is the typical baseline; verify the current requirement with the specific center. Citizenship/work-authorization rules were not confirmed in this pass.
selectivity_note: Typically around 12 fellows per regional center per cohort; exact figures and applicant totals not confirmed in this pass.
pay_note: Program is tuition-free, but STIPENDS ARE NOT GUARANTEED — they are limited in number, need-based, and set independently by each center. Reported ranges: Los Angeles up to $2,200/month plus possible one-time relocation stipend; Bay Area up to $3,000/month; St. Louis typically $500-$1,200/month. Applicants invited to Selection Day are told how to be considered for a stipend. Other centers not confirmed.
cost_note: No tuition or program fee, but fellows without a stipend must self-fund nine months of living costs in an expensive city.

deadlines.note: Applications for the 2027-28 cohort expected to open around September 2026. Exact date not published.
2027-28 deadline not yet published. The 2026-27 cycle's written application was due 11 January 2026; expect a comparable January 2027 date. Deadlines can differ by regional center.

caveat_note: The stipend is the crux: Coro is frequently described as 'funded' but stipends are limited and need-based, so a student could be admitted and still need to cover nine months of rent. Present it as net_neutral at best, and tell users to ask each center directly about stipend availability before accepting. Deadlines and eligibility vary by center — a single national entry is a simplification.

name: Global Health Corps U.S. Leadership Accelerator
summary: A nine-month, tuition-free hybrid leadership program for US-based early-career, non-clinical public health professionals, running September through May. GHC covers retreat travel, lodging and meals — but this US track does not place fellows in salaried jobs.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly. For US-based early-career, NON-CLINICAL public health professionals. The 2026-27 cycle used a priority deadline followed by a final deadline. GHC has historically applied an age cap around 30 for its fellowship programs, but that was NOT confirmed for the current US Leadership Accelerator in this pass — verify. Work authorization / residency requirements unconfirmed.
selectivity_note: Cohort size and applicant totals not confirmed in this pass.
pay_note: The US Leadership Accelerator is tuition-free and GHC covers all program costs including travel to retreat locations, lodging and meals for in-person retreats — but NO living stipend or salary is described for the US track. GHC's separate international fellowship program does provide a monthly living stipend, housing, insurance, visa assistance and travel.
cost_note: No program fee. Fellows must support themselves during the nine months, since this is a hybrid part-time program rather than a paid placement.

deadlines.note: 2027-28 deadline not yet published. The 2026-27 cycle closed 19 March 2026, with priority consideration for applications received by 5 March 2026 and decisions by 30 June 2026. Expect a comparable late-winter 2027 window.

caveat_note: MAJOR CHANGE: Global Health Corps' well-known model used to be a paid year-long placement at a health organization with salary, housing and insurance. The current US-facing offering is a nine-month HYBRID 'Leadership Accelerator' that is tuition-free but appears to pay nothing. Any legacy directory copy describing GHC as a paid fellowship is now wrong. The official overview URL returned 404 — verify the current structure and any age cap directly with GHC before publishing.

name: Venture for America Fellowship
summary: A two-year fellowship placing early-career graduates as full-time salaried employees at startups across a set of US cities, beginning with a summer Training Camp. VFA does not pay fellows — salaries come from the hiring companies.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly. For early-career professionals interested in entrepreneurship, job creation and startup careers. Selection is followed by a 'Match' process in which fellows apply to jobs through a private VFA job portal and must be hired by a partner company; admission to VFA does not by itself guarantee a job. Fellows relocate to one of roughly 13 partner cities. Work authorization requirements not confirmed in this pass.
selectivity_note: Cohort size and applicant totals not confirmed in this pass.
pay_note: There is no cost to the applicant or fellow; fellows are full-time salaried employees and SALARIES ARE PAID BY THE HIRING COMPANIES, not by VFA. Third-party salary aggregators report a range roughly in the $44,000-$74,000 band, but this is crowd-sourced data, not a VFA-published figure — do not present it as an official range.

deadlines.note: VFA runs multiple identical application rounds per cycle (historically around early October, early December and early February, with a fourth round in some years). Specific 2027 dates were listed as TBA at the time of this research. VFA advises applying in an early round to maximize time in the Match process.

caveat_note: Could not retrieve ventureforamerica.org directly (TLS handshake failure) — everything here is from secondary sources and should be verified before publishing. The salary figures are Glassdoor/Indeed estimates, not official. Two structural facts worth surfacing: (1) fellows must separately win a job through the Match, and (2) the two-year commitment is to a startup employer, not to VFA.

name: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange for Young Professionals (CBYX)
operator: Cultural Vistas, funded by the U.S. Department of State and the German Bundestag
summary: A one-year cultural immersion fellowship in Germany combining two months of intensive language school, four months of classroom study, and a five-month professional internship, with a host-family homestay. Airfare, tuition, housing, insurance and a modest monthly stipend are covered.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly to Cultural Vistas. Open to young professionals roughly aged 18.5 to 24 at program start, including those with vocational training, associate's degrees or bachelor's degrees — a four-year degree is not required. No prior German language ability required. Applicants commit to a full 12 months in Germany.
selectivity_note: Roughly 65-75 American participants selected annually (sources differ between 65 and 75), matched with an equal number of German participants. Applicant-pool size not published.
pay_note: Beginning with the 2025-26 program year, participants receive a $150/month personal stipend from the program. Separately covered: round-trip airfare from Washington DC to Germany, two months of intensive language school, four months of study tuition, host-family housing, a monthly living-cost allowance, program-related travel within Germany, and basic health insurance in Germany. The internship portion is not a salaried job.
cost_note: No program fee described, but participants should budget for passport, visa-related costs and personal spending beyond the stipend.
funding_note: 2026-27 program year ran and its applications have closed; Cultural Vistas is collecting contact details for 2027-28 application alerts.

deadlines.note: 2027-28 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED. Historically the deadline has fallen on or around 1 December of the preceding year, with the application opening in late summer/early autumn. Verify on culturalvistas.org; sign up for their alert list.

caveat_note: Automated fetch of the Cultural Vistas program page returned empty content — details here come from search results and university advising pages. Verify the participant count (65 vs 75), the exact age window (18.5-24 is widely cited), and the 2027-28 deadline directly. As a State Department ECA-funded exchange, this program is exposed to federal budget decisions; re-check funding status before each cycle.

name: Humanity in Action Fellowship
summary: An intensive three-to-four-week summer program on human rights, pluralism and minority issues, held in European cities and in Atlanta (the John Lewis Fellowship), followed by an expectation that fellows develop civil-society projects at home. Program costs and accommodation are covered; airfare is generally the fellow's responsibility.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply through Humanity in Action's own online system. Open to students with at least sophomore standing at the application deadline, currently enrolled graduate and PhD students, and individuals who graduated from their program within the last two years. Applicants must be students or recent graduates of US universities and colleges to apply through the US track. There is a $35 application fee.
selectivity_note: The John Lewis Fellowship in Atlanta takes about 30 American and European students. Other program sites have their own cohort sizes; totals and applicant numbers not confirmed.
pay_note: Humanity in Action covers the costs of participation, accommodation and day-to-day local transportation, plus a modest food stipend during the fellowship. It does NOT pay a salary. Fellows are responsible for round-trip airfare; HIA covers airfare for fellows with documented financial need, and additional need-based stipends may be granted.
cost_note: $35 non-refundable application fee, plus round-trip airfare unless a need-based waiver is granted.

deadlines.note: 2027 deadline NOT YET PUBLISHED. Recent cycles have closed in mid-January to mid-March of the program year (e.g. 16 March 2025 at 11:59pm PST for the European programs). The John Lewis Fellowship's 2026 deadline was listed as 'spring 2026, date TBD.' Verify on humanityinaction.org.

caveat_note: Official FAQ page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch — all details are from secondary/advising-office sources and need manual verification. MISMATCH: this is a THREE-TO-FOUR-WEEK SUMMER program, not a year-long post-graduate path; listing it beside year-long fellowships without a duration badge will mislead users. Recent graduates within two years are eligible, so it does fit a gap-year directory as a short add-on.
exclude_reason: A 3-4 week summer program, far too short to function as a gap year.

name: Thomas R. Pickering Foreign Affairs Graduate Fellowship
operator: U.S. Department of State (administered by Howard University)
summary: Funds a two-year master's degree in a field relevant to the Foreign Service, plus paid summer internships, in exchange for a multi-year service commitment as a US Foreign Service Officer. The application cycle has been POSTPONED pending direction from the State Department.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required when running — applicants apply directly. Applicants are college seniors or recent graduates entering a two-year master's program in international affairs, public policy, public administration or a related field. Requires US citizenship, ability to obtain medical and security clearances, and a binding minimum five-year service commitment as a Foreign Service Officer. Historically a minimum 3.2 GPA applied — verify against current rules if the program restarts.
selectivity_note: Historically around 45 fellows per year. Not currently selecting.
pay_note: Historically provided academic funding (tuition, room, board, books, fees) up to an annual cap for two years, plus stipends for two summer internships — one domestic at the State Department, one overseas at a US embassy. Exact current figures not confirmed; program is paused.
funding_note: The 2026 Pickering Fellowship application cycle was POSTPONED pending updates from the U.S. Department of State, and no restart has been announced as of August 2026. Separately, onboarding of already-selected fellows into the Foreign Service stalled: 12 fellows were onboarded in September 2025 and 12 in January 2026, with 28 accepting invitations for an April 2026 class, prompting congressional inquiry. The State Department has said it will meet its contractual obligations to remaining fellows.

deadlines.note: No open cycle. Historically the deadline fell in September. The program advises signing up for its email list for announcements.

caveat_note: DO NOT list as available. Both the application cycle AND the pipeline into the Foreign Service have been disrupted — even past winners have faced long onboarding delays. If you publish this entry at all, pair the 'paused' status with the onboarding-delay context, because the value proposition (a guaranteed path into the Foreign Service) is what is actually in question.

name: Charles B. Rangel International Affairs Graduate Fellowship
operator: U.S. Department of State (administered by Howard University)
summary: Funds a two-year master's degree in a Foreign Service-related field plus paid internships, leading to appointment as a US Foreign Service Officer. The application cycle has been POSTPONED pending direction from the State Department.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required when running — applicants apply directly. For college seniors and graduates entering a two-year US-based master's program in international affairs, public policy, public administration, economics or a related field. Requires US citizenship, medical and security clearance eligibility, and a binding minimum five-year Foreign Service commitment. Historically a minimum 3.2 GPA applied — verify if the program restarts.
selectivity_note: Historically 45 fellows selected annually. Not currently selecting.
pay_note: Historically provided up to approximately $42,000 in annual support toward a two-year master's degree, covering tuition, room, board, books and fees, plus paid congressional and overseas internships. The $42,000 figure is from secondary/advising sources, not verified against the official program site in this pass, and the program is currently paused.
funding_note: The 2026 Rangel application cycle was POSTPONED pending updates from the U.S. Department of State. As with Pickering, onboarding of already-selected fellows into the Foreign Service has been delayed and drew a congressional inquiry. No restart announced as of August 2026.

deadlines.note: No open cycle. Historically the deadline fell in mid-to-late September.

caveat_note: DO NOT list as available. Same disruption pattern as Pickering — cycle postponed and Foreign Service onboarding delayed for existing fellows. The $42,000 annual figure is unverified; drop it or verify before publishing.

name: Donald M. Payne International Development Graduate Fellowship
operator: Formerly U.S. Agency for International Development (administered by Howard University)
summary: Funded a two-year master's degree in international development plus internships, leading to appointment as a USAID Foreign Service Officer. The program was TERMINATED in February 2025 amid the dismantling of USAID and is not accepting applications.
other_eligibility: When running: no campus nomination required. For college seniors and graduates entering a two-year master's in international development or a related field, with US citizenship, clearance eligibility, and a binding service commitment as a USAID Foreign Service Officer. Historically a minimum 3.2 GPA applied.
selectivity_note: Historically around 30 fellows per year. No longer operating.
pay_note: Historically provided up to approximately $96,000 in benefits over two years covering graduate school, internships and professional development. Figure is from secondary/advising sources. Program terminated — no current funding.
funding_note: Terminated as of 27 February 2025 in connection with the shutdown of USAID programs. Members of Congress (including Rep. LaMonica McIver, who wrote to Secretary Rubio in March 2025) have called for reinstatement, but as of August 2026 no cohort is being recruited.

deadlines.note: No open cycle — program terminated. Historically the deadline fell in early November.

caveat_note: DO NOT list as available under any circumstances. Many university advising pages still describe Payne as active, which is a credibility trap — the program was terminated in February 2025. If you keep the entry, keep it explicitly as a 'discontinued' record with the termination date.

name: Herbert Scoville Jr. Peace Fellowship
operator: Herbert Scoville Jr. Peace Fellowship (independent board)
summary: A salaried fellowship placing recent graduates in Washington DC public-interest organizations working on peace, security and arms control. Fellows choose their host organization from a set of participating nonprofits and receive a real monthly salary plus health and professional development support.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly through Submittable. Requires a bachelor's degree (graduate degrees and relevant experience are viewed favorably); the fellowship is aimed at people who have not yet held a full-time professional position in the peace and security field. Fellows must work IN PERSON in Washington DC. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States — verify the current citizenship/work-authorization rule directly, as it was not confirmed in this pass.
selectivity_note: Typically a handful of fellows per cohort, twice a year. Exact numbers and applicant pool not published.
pay_note: $4,283 per month salary. Plus reimbursement of health insurance premiums or health care expenses on a pre-tax basis up to $400/month, reimbursement of travel/moving expenses to Washington DC to begin the fellowship, and $1,500 per fellow for professional development (conferences, language or policy courses). Salary figure from a secondary listing citing scoville.org/benefits/salary — verify the current rate.

deadlines.note: Spring 2027 fellowship application is due in October 2026 — exact date not published on the deadlines page as of this research pass. Spring fellowships start between 15 January and 1 April.
Fall 2027 deadline not yet published. Pattern: the Fall 2026 deadline was 27 February 2026, so expect late February 2027. Fall fellowships start between 15 July and 1 October.

caveat_note: Two intakes a year (spring and fall) with different deadlines — make sure the directory shows both. Fellowship duration (commonly described as six to nine months) was not confirmed on the official pages, so term weeks are left null. Salary figure and the citizenship rule both need a manual check on scoville.org.

name: James C. Gaither Junior Fellows Program
summary: A one-year paid research assistantship at the Carnegie Endowment in Washington DC, working directly with senior scholars on international policy research and writing. Roughly 15 fellows are chosen from nominees put forward by several hundred participating colleges and universities.
other_eligibility: REQUIRES campus nomination — students may NOT apply independently. Only graduating seniors and individuals who graduated during the past academic year are eligible, and only through a participating institution's nominating official (usually the fellowships or national scholarships office). Each participating school forwards a limited number of nominees. Citizenship/work-authorization rules were not confirmed in this pass — verify with Carnegie.
selectivity_note: Approximately 15 one-year fellowships awarded, drawn from nominees submitted by several hundred participating universities and colleges.
pay_note: $4,000 per month stipend, plus a relocation stipend of up to $1,500. The 2027-28 cohort works from 1 September 2027 through 30 June 2028.

deadlines.note: Nominations due FROM THE INSTITUTION to Carnegie by 15 January 2027; acceptances announced by the end of March 2027. Exact time of day not published — the 23:59 here is an assumption, so present this as a date, not a timestamp.

Campus pre-application deadlines run MUCH EARLIER — commonly November or December 2026 (e.g. University of Rhode Island's campus deadline is 1 December 2026, 11:59pm ET), and some schools set deadlines as early as November. Students must contact their fellowships office in autumn 2026.

caveat_note: Campus nomination is mandatory and campus deadlines are the real deadline for students — the January national date is between institutions and Carnegie, not something a student can meet on their own. Time of day for the 15 January deadline is unconfirmed. Citizenship eligibility unverified.

name: Bill Emerson National Hunger Fellowship
summary: An 11-month anti-hunger leadership fellowship combining a roughly five-to-six-month community field placement anywhere in the US with a policy placement in Washington DC. Fellows receive a living allowance, housing support, health insurance and an end-of-service award.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly to the Congressional Hunger Center. The program explicitly recruits for lived experience and commitment to social justice as well as academic background; whether a bachelor's degree is strictly required was NOT confirmed in this pass and should be verified before publishing. Fellows must be able to relocate twice (to a field site, then to Washington DC). Citizenship/work-authorization requirements unconfirmed.
selectivity_note: Cohort size (historically around 20 fellows) and applicant totals not confirmed from official sources in this pass.
pay_note: For 2026-27 the program described financial packages of 'no less than $50,000' over the fellowship. Components cited across sources include a living allowance, an end-of-service cash award, health insurance, relocation stipends, free housing in the host community during the field placement, and a housing stipend to offset DC costs during the policy placement. NOTE: older listings itemize a $14,500 living allowance plus a $3,500 end-of-service award and a $3,500 DC housing stipend, which does not reconcile with a $50,000 package unless the package value includes benefits — verify the current itemization with the Congressional Hunger Center.

deadlines.note: Congressional Hunger Center states applications for the 2027-28 class begin in Fall 2026. Exact opening date not published.
2027-28 deadline not yet published. Recent cycles have closed in mid-January (the 2025 class deadline was 17 January 2025). Expect mid-January 2027; verify on hungercenter.org.

caveat_note: The compensation figures conflict badly between sources ($14,500 living allowance vs 'no less than $50,000' total package) — the hungercenter.org fellows page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so this needs a manual read before publishing any number. Degree requirement is also unconfirmed; the program markets to people with non-traditional backgrounds, so do not assert a bachelor's requirement without checking.

name: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
operator: The Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
summary: Up to $90,000 over two years for immigrants and children of immigrants pursuing any full-time graduate or professional degree in the United States, structured as a $25,000 annual living stipend plus up to $20,000 a year in tuition support. Thirty New Americans are selected each year.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly. Must be 30 or younger as of the application deadline (no minimum age). Must be an immigrant or the child of immigrants: naturalized US citizen, green card holder, asylee or refugee, DACA recipient, or someone who graduated from both high school and college in the United States. Must be planning to enroll full-time in a degree-granting graduate or professional program in the US in the 2027-28 academic year — college seniors are eligible. Open to every field. Selection emphasizes creativity, originality, initiative and sustained accomplishment.
selectivity_note: 30 fellows selected each year. Applicant-pool size not confirmed in this pass.
pay_note: Up to $90,000 total over two years: a $25,000 annual living stipend plus up to $20,000 per year in tuition support, for up to two years of full-time graduate study at any accredited American institution.

deadlines.note: 2027 application deadline: 29 October 2026 at 2:00pm ET. Application is currently open.

caveat_note: The citizenship enum is a poor fit: eligibility is defined by immigration STORY (immigrant or child of immigrants) rather than by status alone, and includes DACA recipients and refugees/asylees — us_citizen_or_lpr undersells it. Surface the full eligibility language rather than the enum. The age-30 cap is hard and measured at the application deadline.

name: Fulbright Public Policy Fellowship
operator: U.S. Department of State Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs (administered by IIE)
summary: Places early- and mid-career professionals in fellowships inside foreign government ministries and public institutions, combining public-sector service with an academic or professional project. Offered in a rotating set of countries across Africa, the Western Hemisphere, and East Asia and the Pacific.
other_eligibility: Campus involvement REQUIRED for enrolled students: applicants currently enrolled at a US institution must apply through their campus Fulbright Program Adviser, whose internal deadline is much earlier than the national one; at-large applicants (not enrolled) apply directly. This award targets EARLY- AND MID-CAREER PROFESSIONALS and historically requires a completed master's or JD (or equivalent) plus relevant professional experience — a fresh bachelor's-only graduate is generally not competitive or eligible. Verify the current degree and experience floor in the award listing for your target country.
selectivity_note: A small number of placements per participating country. Award counts and applicant totals not confirmed in this pass.
pay_note: Fulbright awards of this type typically provide a monthly living stipend set by host country, round-trip international travel, and accident and sickness health benefits. Country-specific stipend amounts were not confirmed in this pass — they vary substantially by post.

deadlines.note: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program 2027-28 national deadline is 6 October 2026 at 5:00pm ET. VERIFY that the Public Policy Fellowship is competed under the Student Program rather than the Fulbright Scholar Program, which runs a different (typically September) deadline — both programs list a 'Public Policy' award and this pass could not disambiguate.

Enrolled students apply through their campus Fulbright Program Adviser; campus deadlines typically fall in AUGUST or EARLY SEPTEMBER 2026, weeks before the national date. At-large (non-enrolled) applicants apply directly and use the national deadline.

caveat_note: BIGGEST RISK IN THIS FILE. Both the official award page (404) and the Fulbright Scholar award page (403) failed to fetch, so which competition this award sits in — and therefore which deadline applies — is unresolved. Participating countries as of recent cycles: Botswana, Ghana, Rwanda, Peru, Colombia, Cambodia, Thailand, Vietnam, Timor-Leste and Fiji, but country rosters rotate annually. Do not publish the deadline without manual verification. Also note the master's-plus-experience bar makes this a poor fit for a typical graduating senior.

name: Young Adults in Global Mission (YAGM)
summary: A one-year international service-learning and faith-formation program placing young adults with companion churches and social service ministries abroad, with training, airfare, room and board, insurance and a small living allowance provided. Volunteers commit to raising financial support toward the roughly $15,000 cost of their placement.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly to the ELCA. Minimum age 21; the upper age limit is cited inconsistently across sources (29 in some ELCA materials, 35 in others) and MUST be verified. A college degree is not strictly required. This is an explicitly faith-based program rooted in Lutheran theology and accompaniment; applicants should expect a faith-formation component and a discernment-oriented interview process. Volunteers are expected to participate in fundraising with a personalized support page.
selectivity_note: Cohort size and applicant totals not published. Country program list has contracted sharply.
pay_note: Volunteers receive training, round-trip airfare, a SMALL living allowance, international health insurance, in-country support, and simple room and board. This is subsistence support, not income — the allowance amount is not published.
cost_note: The ELCA states it costs approximately $15,000 to place one young adult for a year, and volunteers are asked to fundraise toward that cost with ELCA-provided fundraising tools. The volunteer's specific required fundraising minimum was NOT confirmed in this pass — verify, since it is the single most decision-relevant number for applicants.
funding_note: Country programs for 2027-28 are projected as Argentina & Uruguay, Cambodia, Mexico, and the United Kingdom — a substantially shorter list than YAGM's historical roster, which is worth flagging to users.

deadlines.note: Applications for the 2027-28 service year are accepted on a ROLLING basis.

PRIORITY deadline 15 January 2027 — applicants who apply by this date have their placements considered first. Time of day not published; treat as a date. Year inferred from the 2027-28 service year label.
FINAL deadline 1 February 2027. Time of day not published; treat as a date.

caveat_note: Two things to verify before publishing: (1) the upper age limit (29 vs 35 across sources), and (2) the volunteer's actual required fundraising amount, which drives the participant_pays classification. The 2027-28 country list is much shorter than historical — surface it so applicants are not expecting the old range of placements. Note also that this is a religious formation program, not a secular service year.

name: Serving and Learning Together (SALT)
summary: A one-year international service assignment running August to July, with MCC covering travel, housing, food, in-country transport and full medical coverage plus a monthly personal stipend. There is no program fee, and participants are eligible for student loan repayment assistance.
other_eligibility: NO campus nomination required — apply directly to MCC. Open to Canadian and US citizens (so the 'any' value here is wrong in the other direction — it is NOT globally open). A college degree is not required. MCC is an Anabaptist/Mennonite agency and expects participants to share an active Christian faith and be part of a church community; applicants should expect faith-related questions in the application. Age range was not published on the FAQ — verify.
selectivity_note: Cohort size and applicant totals not published.
pay_note: MCC covers all basic needs related to the assignment — travel to and from the assignment, food and household costs, housing, in-country transportation — plus full medical coverage with no co-pay, vacation days, and orientation and re-entry travel. Participants receive a monthly stipend for personal items such as clothing, vacations and haircuts; the AMOUNT IS NOT PUBLISHED on MCC's FAQ. Participants are also eligible for student loan repayment assistance.
cost_note: No program fee to participate in SALT. Participants do pay for their own pre-service medical exams, optional dental/optical exams, passport, visa expenses and vaccinations.

deadlines.note: MCC states that only applications received before 15 February are guaranteed consideration for a placement starting the following August. Applications open each fall. Time of day not published — treat as a date, not a timestamp. Year inferred for the August 2027 start.
MCC begins accepting applications each fall for terms starting the following August; expect a September 2026 opening for the 2027-28 term.

caveat_note: Citizenship enum is a bad fit — SALT is open to US AND Canadian citizens only, so neither 'us_citizen' nor 'any' is accurate; display the real rule. Monthly stipend amount is not published anywhere MCC-official, so do not quote a figure. Age range unpublished. Like YAGM this is an explicitly faith-based program with a church-participation expectation — that belongs in the user-facing description, not buried.
